title: LAION-BVD: A 13-Million-Hour Open Video Dataset for Multimodal Pre-training
claim: Our dataset is far larger than existing ones, and models trained on it perform strongly and scale well across modalities.
layout: 3 panels, left-to-right, bar charts then scatter-with-trend lines, warm/green palettes
description: A three-panel row of plots. The left panel is a bar chart comparing dataset sizes. Each bar has its value printed above it, and the LAION-BVD (Total) bar at 13.5M is highlighted in a darker gold and towers over the pale bars for the other datasets, including InternVid at 760.3k. LAION-BVD (Captioned) is shown at 168k. The middle panel, titled ViCLIP, is a grouped bar chart of accuracy for Average Retrieval and Average Classification, with four training datasets in a gold and tan palette: DataComp-1B, InternVid-10M-FLT, BVD-V-10M and BVD-V-50M. The right panel, titled CLAP, is a scatter plot with fitted trend lines of accuracy against model size. It compares LAION-Audio (light green crosses) with BVD-A-10M (darker green dots), and the BVD-A-10M line sits higher. Dashed grid lines run behind the bars and points. The eye goes first to the tall highlighted bar on the left.
caption: LAION-BVD is an open web video dataset at unprecedented scale. It facilitates strong downstream performance for multimodal pre-training. Left: dataset scale in comparison with existing video datasets (Total: BVD-RAW, Captioned: BVD-V-55M). Right: average downstream performance of ViCLIP [146] (video-text, Table 6) and scaling trends of CLAP [151] (audio-text, Table 7) on standard benchmarks. These results demonstrate that LAION-BVD serves as valuable training data across both video and audio modalities.
abstract: We present LAION-BVD (LAION - Big Video Dataset), a large-scale open video dataset for multimodal learning, which contains 1.3B platform-specific video URLs collected from CommonCrawl. From these, we download 80M videos with a total duration of 13.5 million hours. The dataset is designed for multimodal pre-training across the video, audio, and image modalities. Using content-aware scene detection, we extract clips for which we synthetically generate video and audio captions. Models trained on these data achieve competitive performance on standard video-text and audio-text benchmarks, with consistent improvements as training or model scale increases. Additionally, we explore video frames as an alternative source of image-text data by extracting scene-changing frames. These frames exhibit a visual distribution distinct from standard web image corpora, and models trained on this dataset achieve strong image-text retrieval performance. We release LAION-BVD to the research community. It significantly expands open access to multimodal videos at an unprecedented scale.
